description: Replace the dual Issue/Epic identity and Epic-owned membership model with Project-scoped number identities, Issue-owned current affiliation, one-aggregate durable coordination, and canonical producer-family event lineage.

tasks.title: Introduce scoped Issue/Epic keys and migrate persisted references
tasks.description: Introduce strong IssueKey(ProjectId, IssueNumber) and EpicKey(ProjectId, EpicNumber) values plus one lossless Orleans grain-key codec. Build an idempotent current-state migration from random IssueId/EpicId references to Project + number across Issue/Epic rows and every owning reference (comments, prerequisites, workflow/profile metadata, inbox, sessions, projections, attachments/associations where applicable). Preserve existing current relationships and distinguish equal numbers in different Projects. Keep any temporary translation adapter private to this migration sequence; it is not part of the target model and must be removed by T-002/T-008.
acceptanceCriteria: IssueKey and EpicKey encode/decode both components through one shared typed GrainKey codec; call sites do not hand-concatenate scoped keys.
Persistence has canonical ProjectId + IssueNumber / EpicNumber references for every current-state relationship that previously used IssueId/EpicId.

A migration spec seeds Issues/Epics plus comments, prerequisites, WorkflowRun/profile/session/inbox/projection references, runs the migration twice, and proves all relationships resolve to the same Project-scoped resources without duplicates.
Two Projects may both contain Issue 42 and Epic 7 without actor, query, or persistence collisions.
No migration transaction combines two aggregate state transitions; schema/data migration may transform stored rows but runtime aggregate commands remain outside it.
Focused server migration, key-codec, and query specs pass; server builds with TreatWarningsAsErrors.
tasks.output: Typed scoped keys/codec, EF row/reference migration, current-state migration specs, and compiling server storage/query foundations for number-only identity.
tasks.notes: Known direct owners from the planning audit include IssueRow/EpicRow, IssueCommentRow, IssueWorkflowProfile, InboxItemRow, WorkflowRun metadata/WorkIssueRef, workflow artifacts/profile lookups, Issue/Epic event source/index paths, AgentSession origin labels, and API/read projections; IssuePrerequisiteRow is already number-shaped but still needs scoped-key verification. Audit again before changing columns. A database surrogate is disallowed if domain code or contracts can observe it as Issue/Epic identity. Do not rewrite historical CloudEvent envelopes; supporting current-query indexes may be migrated separately.

tasks.title: Cut the server domain and APIs to number-only Issue/Epic identity
tasks.description: Switch Issue/Epic domain entities, grains, repositories, queriers, API routes/DTOs, profiles, and server-side commands/events to IssueKey/EpicKey and Project-scoped number references. Remove random id creation, id resolvers, id-based grain access, id fields, and dual id/number server contracts. Resource paths and CloudEvents sources use Project + number. Update affected fakes and specs to build scoped identities directly.
acceptanceCriteria: Creating an Issue or Epic allocates only its Project-local number and returns no random IssueId/EpicId.
Issue/Epic domain state, DTOs, grains, queries, routes, profiles, domain commands, and current-state events use Project + number as the canonical identity.
Issue/Epic resource and CloudEvents source paths include ProjectId and number and require no alias lookup.
Production server code no longer creates or resolves random IssueId/EpicId; migration-only input readers are removed once current state is converted.
Cross-Project same-number API and grain specs prove isolation.
Focused Issue/Epic API, grain, query, and profile specs pass; server unit/spec projects build cleanly.
tasks.output: Number-only Issue/Epic server domain, actors, API contracts, queries, profiles, event sources, and updated focused specs with no id alias layer.
tasks.notes: This is a breaking cutover. Do not preserve id fields in DTOs or add fallback route resolution. Keep independently identified resources such as WorkflowRunId, SessionId, AgentId, RunnerId, ProjectId, and EventId unchanged.

tasks.title: Move Epic membership authority into Issue and rebuild progression
tasks.description: Add nullable EpicNumber to Issue as the only current affiliation fact. Implement idempotent AssignEpic and expected-number RemoveEpic with IssueEpicChanged(previous,current). Rewrite link/unlink/move so Epic validates and commands Issue without sharing a transaction. Migrate current affiliation from old membership rows, then remove EpicIssueRow/EpicActiveIssue and all dual writes. Rebuild Epic member/progress/candidate queries over Issue state and use guarded Issue.TryStartFromEpic commands. Durable Issue reactions recompute affected Epics and refresh active Workflow context from current Issue state.
acceptanceCriteria: Issue commits EpicNumber changes and IssueEpicChanged in one Issue-only transaction; no Epic or WorkflowRun state participates.
Link is idempotent across lost replies and later Epic closure; new links to closed Epic are rejected; expected-number unlink cannot clear a newer move.
Moving A -> B is one Issue state change with no two-owner intermediate state.
Epic membership/progress/startable candidates come from current Issue state; Epic owns only lifecycle/progression state.
done revival, closed rejection, reopen, empty/all-terminal completion, sequential advance, prerequisites, and sub-Issue exclusions retain their product behavior on the new model.
Out-of-order/repeated IssueEpicChanged handlers re-read current Issue and never regress Epic or Workflow context.
Migration specs preserve current affiliation and remove old membership/active rows; no runtime code reads or writes those tables afterward.
Focused Issue membership, Epic lifecycle/progression, transaction failure, and durable redelivery specs pass.
tasks.output: Issue-owned EpicNumber model, affiliation commands/events/reactions, derived Epic queries/progression, old membership storage removal, migration and crash/redelivery specs.
tasks.notes: Do not replace the old rows with a new relation aggregate or generic OwnerRef. Epic may synchronously call Issue, but Issue must not synchronously call back into Epic on that stack; reverse progress is event-driven.

tasks.title: Replace Workflow binding and lineage revision with durable EnsureStarted
tasks.description: Simplify Issue -> Workflow coordination to the durable IssueWorkStarted fact. Issue allocates/stores WorkflowRunId and raises its event in an Issue-only transaction. The handler re-reads current Issue and calls WorkflowRun.EnsureStarted(runId, {ProjectId, IssueNumber, EpicNumber?}); WorkflowRun creates/starts idempotently in its own transaction. Store only that small context and refresh it from current Issue after affiliation events. Remove AwaitingBinding, WorkflowBindingPending, EnsureWorkflowBinding/confirmation, IssueLineageVersion/LineageVersion ordering, related status/control/runner/web handling, migrations, and tests for the superseded protocol. Preserve the reviewer fix that rejects a dirty WorkflowGrain activation before Start mutates stale state.
acceptanceCriteria: Issue start transaction writes only Issue state plus IssueWorkStarted and never creates/locks WorkflowRun.
EnsureStarted creates and starts exactly the allocated run and is idempotent across duplicate delivery and lost replies.
Handler no-ops when a delayed event no longer identifies the Issue's current active run.
WorkflowRun context is exactly ProjectId, IssueNumber, EpicNumber?; affiliation refresh uses current Issue state and no revision field.
Workflow result commands carry expected WorkflowRunId so old completion/failure cannot change a newer Issue run.
AwaitingBinding, pending/confirmation commands, lineage revision fields, special control guards, runner statuses, and web statuses are absent from the target code.
Crash-window specs cover before creation, after creation before reply, redelivery after acknowledgement failure, context refresh ordering, and stale Workflow results.
WorkflowGrain Start still calls RejectIfRunReloadRequired before mutation; its state-save-failure regression passes.
tasks.output: IssueWorkStarted handler + WorkflowRun.EnsureStarted, minimal run context, expected-run result guards, removal of binding/revision protocol, and focused recovery specs.
tasks.notes: A WorkflowRun may be temporarily absent after Issue commits; that is a normal durable-process interval, not a new persisted Workflow status. Do not reintroduce discovery scans or binding markers.

tasks.title: Adopt canonical lineage extensions and producer-family conformance
tasks.description: Replace issueid/epicid/issueno/epicno with projectid + issue/epic number lineage. Stamp WorkflowRun, Issue, Epic, AgentSession, Runner producers and the inbox-synthesized event from producer-owned state/metadata only; use structural Stage inspection. Reduce EventCatalog back to stable type names and replace per-type RequiredAttributes/EnvelopeConformance/CatalogOnlyTypes with producer-family conformance used by real production-path specs. Remove catalog entries that were accidentally presented as produced facts only when they are not stable reserved protocol names; otherwise retain them strictly as type constants without fake conformance.
acceptanceCriteria: WorkflowRun stamps projectid/workflowrunid plus local issue/epic and structural stage; Issue stamps projectid/issue plus local epic; Epic stamps projectid/epic.
AgentSession, Runner, and inbox paths stamp the applicable canonical context defined by the delta spec; optional values are omitted, never empty.
No append/synthesis path queries another aggregate to gather lineage.
No new producer emits issueid, epicid, issueno, or epicno.
EventCatalog has no required-attribute registry; CatalogOnlyTypes and per-type bypass logic are removed.
Producer-family conformance covers every real producer and serializable domain-event variant, including negative missing/empty cases.
Stage conformance follows event structure, including feedback-requested and excluding non-stage artifact/run events.
Focused transactional append/synthesis and conformance specs pass.
tasks.output: Canonical number-only lineage builders at all producers, structural Stage logic, simplified EventCatalog, producer-family conformance helper/specs, and obsolete registry removal.
tasks.notes: Historical envelopes are not rewritten and need not satisfy the new shape. Conformance must test actual append/synthesis paths, not merely helper dictionaries or catalog declarations.

tasks.title: Reconcile server lineage consumers and current-state integrations
tasks.description: Update server subscriptions, Epic progression reactions, Inbox, Hermes payloads, Session origin metadata, Workflow profile/context lookup, and other current-state consumers to Project + issue/epic number and canonical envelope context. Routing decisions use envelope extensions first and payload remains unchanged display/audit data. Remove legacy issueno/epicno and issueid/epicid fallbacks from target paths. Ensure durable handlers re-read current Issue only when executing a domain reaction; matcher/dispatcher routing itself remains envelope-only.
acceptanceCriteria: Epic/Issue/Workflow subscription handlers resolve scoped number identity from canonical envelope context and do not depend on payload identity.
Inbox-synthesized events inherit current canonical context and no longer carry IssueId.
Hermes current payload exposes issueNumber and optional epicNumber, not issueId/epicId.
Workflow-origin AgentSession metadata/events carry issue/epic number context where present; agent-origin sessions keep their independent agent/session identities.
Payload/envelope disagreement specs route by envelope while preserving payload bytes/object for display.
No server consumer retains issueno/epicno or random Issue/Epic id fallback in current paths.
Focused subscription, Inbox, Hermes, Session, and profile specs pass.
tasks.output: Canonical server consumer/subscription routing, Inbox/Hermes/Session/profile integration changes, removal of legacy reads, and disagreement/redelivery specs.
tasks.notes: Domain reaction handlers may query current Issue before a command; event matching and dispatch selection may not. Do not mutate payload to smuggle routing identity into existing client shapes.

tasks.title: Cut CLI and Web to scoped numbers and envelope-first routing
tasks.description: Update CLI and Web Issue/Epic resource contracts to use Project-scoped numbers only. Remove id-or-number inputs and id fields from client types, query keys, routes, fixtures, and displays. Ensure Epic link/unlink/start/pause/resume/done/close/reopen take Epic number and Issue number in Project scope. Update Web event-envelope/timeline logic so canonical extensions determine routing while payload remains display data.
acceptanceCriteria: CLI Issue/Epic commands send scoped numbers and expose no id-or-number ambiguity; Epic reopen is available with the same number contract.
Web Issue/Epic API clients, entity types, query keys, links, and forms carry ProjectId + number and no random id identity.
Web timeline uses extensions.issue/extensions.epic before payload identity and preserves the original payload.
Cross-Project same-number client/query tests do not share cache entries or routes.
No current CLI/Web fixture or production path uses issueid, epicid, issueno, or epicno.
CLI tests, Web typecheck, and Web test suite pass.
tasks.output: Number-only CLI/Web contracts and commands, Project-scoped query/routes, Epic reopen CLI, envelope-first timeline routing, and updated tests/fixtures.
tasks.notes: The product is pre-compatibility. Do not retain id aliases or dual cache keys. Keep Project selection explicit because number alone is not globally unique.

tasks.title: Remove superseded model and verify aggregate recovery end to end
tasks.description: Perform the final invariant audit and delete all superseded candidate code, schema, migrations, tests, and documentation fragments: random Issue/Epic ids, membership/active rows, affiliation caches owned by Epic, AwaitingBinding/pending/confirmation, lineage revisions, per-type catalog lineage registry, catalog-only bypasses, and legacy extension aliases. Add end-to-end durable dispatcher specs for the link/move/start/complete crash and ordering matrix. Validate the current-state migration and all server/CLI/Web/runner contracts as one cutover.
acceptanceCriteria: A production-code audit finds no random IssueId/EpicId identity, Epic membership/active row, AwaitingBinding/binding marker, lineage revision, CatalogOnlyTypes, or legacy lineage alias outside explicit historical migration descriptions.
Transaction-boundary specs prove Epic commands never write Issue/WorkflowRun, Issue commands never write Epic/WorkflowRun, and WorkflowRun commands never read/write Issue in the same transaction.

Dispatcher specs cover lost link reply, failed Epic recompute, out-of-order affiliation events, Issue start before run creation, EnsureStarted lost reply, and delayed old Workflow result without dead letters or state regression.
Current-state migration is idempotent and leaves no orphan references; historical event rows remain untouched.
git diff --check passes; server build/test, CLI tests, Web typecheck/tests, runner typecheck/tests, architecture tests, and the repository full npm test pass.
OpenSpec progress/self-review describe the implemented target rather than the superseded candidate.
tasks.output: Clean number-only/Issue-owned implementation, deleted obsolete protocol, aggregate transaction and dispatcher recovery specs, migration proof, and complete validation record.
tasks.notes: Do not mark this task complete by excluding legacy types from an audit. Remove them or document a truly independent identity with a different domain owner. Preserve unrelated reviewer guard fixes and user changes.
